A ` ```git-sandbox ` block becomes a Git repository that runs in the
reader's browser. Learners type real `git` commands, and a checklist you
write in YAML ticks itself off as they go. Nothing is installed or
uploaded, and a reload starts the exercise over.

Most boxes on this page come with the block that made them.
The [README](https://github.com/jansim/quarto-git-sandbox#readme) has the
full reference, and a [reveal.js deck](example-revealjs.html) shows boxes
on slides. Source code and issues are at
[github.com/jansim/quarto-git-sandbox](https://github.com/jansim/quarto-git-sandbox).

## Install

```bash
quarto add jansim/quarto-git-sandbox
```

Then list the filter in your document's front matter:

```yaml
filters:
  - git-sandbox
```

## The parts of a box

![](images/sandbox-tour.png)

- **Terminal.** The prompt shows the folder and the current branch. `help`
  lists the supported commands, and the up arrow recalls earlier ones.
  The **Editor** tab next to it opens files for editing.
- **Tasks.** Your checklist. A task ticks once its condition is true and
  stays ticked.
- **Undo** takes back the last command that changed anything. **Reset**
  starts the exercise over.
- **Panels** below the terminal, redrawn after every command:
  - **File Status**: working directory, staging area and repository, with
    each file shown where it currently is.
  - **Changes**: a diff of everything since the last commit.
  - **History**: the commit graph. The chevron on a commit shows what it changed.
  - **Remote**: your history and the remote's, side by side. This tab
    appears once a remote exists.

This box starts with two commits:

```git-sandbox
id: anatomy
title: A tour of the git box
prompt: "~/demo-project $"
intro: |
  This repository already has two commits. Run a few commands and watch
  the panels below; every one of them updates after each command.
  Type {y}help{/} to see what the sandbox supports.
hints: [git status, git log --oneline, 'echo "A new line." >> README.md', git diff, git add ., 'git commit -m "Extend the README"']
done-note: That is the whole feedback loop. Every command updates every panel. Your lessons ride on top of it.
seed: |
  git init
  echo "# Demo project" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add the README"
  echo "library(tidyverse)" > analysis.R
  git add .
  git commit -m "Start the analysis"
tasks:
  - text: Ask where things stand with `git status`
    when: ran /^\s*git\s+status/
  - text: Change a file and find it in the Changes panel
    when: not clean
  - text: Stage it and watch it move to the staging area in the diagram
    when: staged
  - text: Commit it and watch the history graph grow
    when: commits >= 3
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="The block for this box"}

## A minimal exercise

All you need is a `title` and some `tasks`. Without a `seed`, the box
starts as an empty folder with nothing tracked.

````markdown
```git-sandbox
id: minimal
title: A minimal exercise
prompt: "~/scratch $"
intro: |
  This box was authored in a few lines of YAML. It starts as an
  empty folder; nothing is tracked yet.
tasks:
  - text: Turn the folder into a repository
    when: repo
  - text: Commit a file
    when: commits >= 1
```
````

```git-sandbox
id: minimal
title: A minimal exercise
prompt: "~/scratch $"
intro: |
  This box was authored in a few lines of YAML. It starts as an
  empty folder; nothing is tracked yet.
tasks:
  - text: Turn the folder into a repository
    when: repo
  - text: Commit a file
    when: commits >= 1
```

- `intro` is printed as terminal output, so Markdown does not apply. Use
  `{y}…{/}` for yellow, `{g}` for green, `{r}` for red, `{b}` for blue and
  `{w}` for bold.
- `hints` are buttons that put a command in the prompt (the first box has
  them). In `[...]` lists, put single quotes around any entry that
  contains a double quote: `'git commit -m "First note"'`.
- `prompt` names the project folder, which `git init` and `pwd` also
  print.

## Checking progress with `when:`

Each task's `when:` is a condition on the repository's state. The tasks in
this box show the conditions that check them:

```git-sandbox
id: when-playground
title: The when-language playground
prompt: "~/demo-project $"
intro: |
  Each task below shows the {y}when:{/} condition that checks it.
  Complete them in any order.
done-note: Every condition here is plain YAML. See the README for the full list.
seed: |
  git init
  echo "# Demo project" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add the README"
tasks:
  - text: 'Create a branch called `docs` (`when: branch docs`)'
    when: branch docs
  - text: 'Add a file mentioning Setup (`when: file SETUP.md contains "Setup"`)'
    when: file SETUP.md contains "Setup"
  - text: 'Bring it back (`when: on main and merged docs into main`)'
    when: on main and merged docs into main
```

The full vocabulary:

```yaml
when: repo                           # git init has been run
when: staged                         # something is staged
when: clean                          # nothing uncommitted or untracked
when: commits >= 3                   # also >, <, <=, ==
when: commits on docs >= 2           # reachable from the `docs` branch
when: branch docs                    # the branch exists
when: on main                        # HEAD is on `main`
when: detached                       # HEAD is on a commit, not a branch
when: merged docs into main          # a real merge brought `docs` into `main`
when: merge commit                   # some commit has two parents
when: merging                        # a merge stopped on conflicts
when: conflicts                      # files still need resolving
when: file SETUP.md                  # the file exists
when: file SETUP.md contains "Setup" # ...and holds that text (or a /regex/)
when: ran /git\s+log\s+--oneline/    # the learner typed a matching command
when: remote                         # a remote is configured
when: pushed                         # every commit on the branch is on the remote
```

Combine conditions with `and`, `or`, `not` and parentheses. `and` binds
more tightly than `or`.

```yaml
when: on spike and commits on spike >= 2
when: not branch spike and ran /git\s+branch\s+-[dD]/
```

Prefer conditions on state over `ran`. `commits >= 1` is true however the
learner made the commit, but `ran "git commit"` fails as soon as someone
types it differently. A condition that cannot be read shows its error next
to the task, so you never need the browser console.

## Examples

### Branch and merge

A `seed` runs commands before the learner arrives. This one leaves a
`forecast` branch that has diverged from `main`, so merging it makes a
real merge commit, drawn as a hollow circle.

```git-sandbox
id: merge-flow
title: Merge a diverged branch
prompt: "~/sales-analysis $"
intro: |
  A colleague worked on the {y}forecast{/} branch while main moved on.
  Run {y}git log --oneline{/} on each branch, then merge and watch the graph.
done-note: Two lanes, one merge commit. Seeds let every learner start from exactly this moment.
seed: |
  git init
  echo "# Sales analysis" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add the project README"
  git checkout -b forecast
  echo "arima(sales)" > forecast.R
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add a first forecast model"
  echo "tune the model" >> forecast.R
  git add .
  git commit -m "Tune the forecast parameters"
  git checkout main
tasks:
  - text: Commit a change on `main` so the two branches diverge
    when: commits on main >= 2 and not merged main into forecast
  - text: Merge `forecast` into `main`
    when: on main and merged forecast into main
  - text: Confirm the history now contains a merge commit with two parents
    when: merge commit
  - text: 'Tidy up: delete the merged branch with `git branch -d forecast`'
    when: not branch forecast and ran /git\s+branch\s+-[dD]/
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="The seed"}
```yaml
seed: |
  git init
  echo "# Sales analysis" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add the project README"
  git checkout -b forecast
  echo "arima(sales)" > forecast.R
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add a first forecast model"
  echo "tune the model" >> forecast.R
  git add .
  git commit -m "Tune the forecast parameters"
  git checkout main
```
:::

If a seed command fails, the box shows an error, so learners never start
from a half-built repository. **Reset** runs the seed again.

### Resolve a merge conflict

A conflicting merge stops just as it does in git: the file gets conflict
markers and the prompt shows `(main|MERGING)`. The learner fixes the file,
runs `git add`, then `git commit`. `git merge --abort` cancels the merge.

```git-sandbox
id: conflict-flow
title: Resolve a merge conflict
prompt: "~/sales-analysis $"
intro: |
  You and a colleague both retitled {y}README.md{/}. Merge their
  {y}title{/} branch and see what git does with two edits to one line.
done-note: A conflict is git asking you to decide. Take the markers out, `git add`, commit.
seed: |
  git init
  echo "# Sales analysis" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add the project README"
  git checkout -b title
  echo "# Sales analysis 2026" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Retitle for the new year"
  git checkout main
  echo "# Quarterly sales analysis" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Say which sales"
tasks:
  - text: Merge `title` into `main` and read the `CONFLICT` message
    when: conflicts
  - text: Edit `README.md` down to the line you want, then mark it resolved with `git add`
    when: merging and not conflicts and not file README.md contains "<<<<<<<"
  - text: Conclude the merge with `git commit`
    when: merged title into main and merge commit
```

### Push and pull with a remote

`git remote add origin <url>` creates a mock remote inside the page and
shows the **Remote** tab. Push, fetch and pull work as they do with a real
remote, including the rejection when the remote has commits you don't.

The seed below uses `rewind 1`, a command that only seeds need: it moves
the local branch back one commit after the push, so the remote is one
commit ahead, as if a colleague had pushed in the meantime.

```git-sandbox
id: remote-flow
title: Pull, work, push
prompt: "~/sales-analysis $"
intro: |
  While you were away, a colleague pushed a commit to the shared repository.
  Compare the {y}History{/} tab with the {y}Remote{/} tab: the remote is ahead.
  (Try {y}git push{/} first if you want to see what a rejected push looks like.)
done-note: Pull, work, push, and the two graphs agree again. The rewind trick in the seed is what made the remote start out ahead.
seed: |
  git init
  git remote add origin https://github.com/acme/sales-analysis
  echo "# Sales analysis" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add the project README"
  git push -u origin main
  echo "arima(sales)" > forecast.R
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add a first forecast model"
  git push
  rewind 1
tasks:
  - text: Ask the remote what is new with `git fetch`, and watch `origin/main` move in your history
    when: ran /^\s*git\s+fetch\s*$/
  - text: Bring the colleague's commit into your branch with `git pull`
    when: commits on main >= 2
  - text: 'Do your own work: create a file, stage it, commit it'
    when: commits on main >= 3
  - text: Publish it with `git push`, and check the two graphs agree
    when: commits on main >= 3 and pushed
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple" title="The seed"}
```yaml
seed: |
  git init
  git remote add origin https://github.com/acme/sales-analysis
  echo "# Sales analysis" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add the project README"
  git push -u origin main                  # the first push sets the upstream
  echo "arima(sales)" > forecast.R
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add a first forecast model"
  git push                                 # the colleague's commit
  rewind 1                                 # gone locally, still on the remote
```
:::

### The commit tree

`tree-view: true` opens a commit tree beside the box, drawn in the style of
[Learn Git Branching](https://learngitbranching.js.org/). Commits are named
`C0`, `C1`, … in the order they were made, and `main*` marks the branch
`HEAD` is on. Changes are animated as they happen. By default the tree
stays closed behind the graph button in the box's header, and
`tree-view: false` removes that button.

```git-sandbox
id: tree-flow
title: Branch, commit, merge
prompt: "~/sales-analysis $"
tree-view: true
intro: |
  Watch the {y}Commit tree{/} on the right as you go.
  Each command moves something there: commits, branch labels, or HEAD's {y}*{/}.
done-note: That is the shape of every feature branch, drawn one commit at a time.
seed: |
  git init
  echo "# Sales analysis" > README.md
  git add .
  git commit -m "Add the project README"
  echo "sales <- read_csv('sales.csv')" > load.R
  git add .
  git commit -m "Load the sales data"
tasks:
  - text: Create and switch to a branch called `report`, and watch `main*` hand its star over
    when: on report
  - text: Commit on `report` and watch its label move down with the new commit
    when: commits on report >= 3
  - text: Go back to `main` and merge `report` into it
    when: on main and merged report into main
```

### Two boxes, one repository

`share: <id>` turns a box into a second view of another box's repository.
The files and history are shared, but each box has its own title, tasks and
layout. This box shares `tree-flow` above, so work done in one appears in
the other.

```git-sandbox
id: tree-flow-view
share: tree-flow
title: The same repository, later on
intro: |
  This box shares its repository with "Branch, commit, merge" above.
  Anything you did there is already here.
panel-tabs: [history]
tasks:
  - text: Delete the merged `report` branch
    when: merged report into main and not branch report
```

````markdown
```git-sandbox
share: tree-flow
title: The same repository, later on
panel-tabs: [history]
```
````

A box with `share` has no `seed` of its own. **Reset** in either box
starts the shared repository over.

## Showing less

Each part of the box beyond the terminal can be removed or folded away:

```yaml
editor: false          # no Editor tab
tree-view: false       # no commit tree (true opens it, toggle is the default)
panels: true           # panels always open (toggle adds a fold button, false removes them)
panel-tabs: [history]  # which panels to offer: files, changes, history, remote
```
